market: This review falls on a weekend (Sat Aug 1) — PSX is closed, no new session data since Friday Jul 31's close. That Friday session actually reversed the week's slide: KSE-100 closed at 176,096.11, up ~0.31% on the day, after an early rally of over 1,200 points on renewed buying across automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, fertiliser, E&P, OMCs and power generation — ending a four-session losing streak driven by Middle East war jitters and the oil-price spike. Against the Jan 23, 2026 all-time high of 189,556, the drawdown still sits at roughly 7.1% — unchanged from before the rebound and still clear of the 10% line that would trigger deploying the AICF/MICF cash reserve. SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% at the Jul 27 MPC meeting; S&P Global's upgrade of Pakistan to 'B' (from 'B-') earlier this month remains a supportive medium-term backdrop. No holding-specific news surfaced over the weekend. On holdings: EFERT's H1 2026 results remain as confirmed Jul 30 from the PSX filing — consolidated H1 profit Rs 7.12B (-15.9% YoY), EPS Rs 5.33 (vs Rs 6.34), standalone entity worse (-34.6% YoY), cushioned by a one-off Rs 1.8B SIDC remeasurement gain; a genuine earnings decline confirming the glut thesis. The board still declared a Rs 1.75/share (17.5%) interim dividend, record date Monday Aug 10, 2026 (book closure Aug 11-12) — now 9 days out. AVN closed Friday at Rs 31.38 (down slightly on the day even as the broader market rallied), and holdings data (index.html DEFAULT_HOLDINGS) still shows the full 24,500-share position — the sell-half plan flagged Jul 27 and due that same day has now gone five trading days without execution across fourteen consecutive reviews, with the market itself closed until Monday; there's no new AVN-specific reason to wait, execute at Monday's open. AVN's next earnings report is confirmed for Sep 2, 2026. Technical note: the fund NAV side of the price feed (ASSF, AKDISSF, NISIF, NISF, MIF, AICF, MICF, AKDISIF) has now been frozen identical for eight straight days since Jul 24 — increasingly looks like a stalled MUFAP scraper rather than flat markets (check scripts/fetch_prices.py's fund-scrape path); doesn't change today's calls since fund prices are directionally stale rather than wrong.
